localFinding: The graph planner selected MPOLYGON and its targets, but final DXF record-identity validation whitelisted HATCH and rejected the valid MPOLYGON publication.

changes.summary: Include MPOLYGON in HATCH boundary graph gathering, entity inventory, and final MPOLYGON DXF record-identity validation.

Run the existing 16 identity/owner mutation negatives for both HATCH and MPOLYGON, and exercise MPOLYGON positive graph publication plus missing-target/no-replacement controls for ASCII and Binary DXF.
Register the --hatch-references graph selector as a dedicated narrow fast CTest.

Keep generated AC1018/AC1024 HATCH and MPOLYGON readback plus DWG-to-ASCII/Binary-DXF and imported-DXF-to-version-matched-DWG roundtrips, exact path-reference/target remapping, following-entity sentinels, and source-model identity restoration.
Refine 7N.4/7F.1 readiness, record the MPOLYGON identity failure and passing graph composition slice, and preserve unqualified route boundaries.

positive: MPOLYGON and HATCH graph publication with three generated boundary targets
AC1018 and AC1024 generated DWG readback with path counts 2/0/1
DWG-to-ASCII and DWG-to-Binary DXF path-reference roundtrip with remapped handles
ASCII/Binary DXF import to version-matched DWG write/readback for HATCH and MPOLYGON with newly assigned DWG target handles
Source DXF entity handles, owner handles, and per-path reference lists are restored after DWG serialization
negative: Missing MPOLYGON target refuses publication and preserves a pre-existing destination in ASCII and Binary DXF
The same 16 duplicate/ambiguous/owner/identity mutations reject for both HATCH and MPOLYGON
semanticBoundaries: MPOLYGON group 71 remains solid-fill state, not HATCH associativity
Graph closure does not establish geometric path agreement or native edit/recompute behavior
Generated codec roundtrip is not independent native consumer qualification

narrowCTests.summary: 3/3 passed; focused boundary-reference, graph mutation, and DXF fixture gates

remainingBoundaries: Geometric boundary agreement and native associative edit/recompute remain external consumer semantics, not codec graph-closure claims.
The LibreCAD bundled fork still needs its explicit port and consumer compile/readback.
